basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 1-4.' and it opens 'VERS. 1-4.-- Hic est liber generationis Adam, in | die qua creavit Deus hominem; ad'. The printing's caput is stale here, its marker for this chapter being missing, so the chapter is taken from the lemma, whose best match anywhere in Genesis falls on the very verse the printing numbers.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 1-4.-- Hic est liber generationis Adam, in | die qua creavit Deus hominem; ad similitudinem Dei fecit illum, et reliqua usque: et vocavit nomen eorum Adam in die qua creati sunt. Bene ait, et vocavit nomina eorum Adam, id est, homo. Hominis autem nomen tam viro quam feminae convenit.
